short_answer: SportsMemo is a real, long running pick marketplace. Its terms give a Las Vegas address and Nevada law, and its refund page names Wager Talk Media, LP as the parent company. WagerTalk announced it had bought SportsMemo in August 2018. In that narrow sense the business is legitimate.

Whether its experts win is a different question. The site shows a 7 day profit leaderboard and blurbs such as "25-10-1 over his last 36 plays here at SportsMemo." Those numbers come from the seller, and the page of yesterday's plays asked us to log in. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick that we could check.

Prices are low per play, often $5, which limits what a buyer can lose on the picks themselves. Treat the records as marketing, not proof, and log every play yourself with the line and time you got it.

guarantee: SportsMemo offers no win guarantee. The FAQ says "No picks or predictions are guaranteed" and that all sales are final. The refund policy adds that "Once a product or service has been purchased, delivered, and/or viewed, no refunds will be issued."

The terms say the buyer's exclusive remedy is "a refund of the price paid or replacement of our products, at our option." We found no free extra time or credit offer on the pages we read. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: Each blurb picks its own window: the last 36 plays, since mid October, nine in a row, one past season. A window chosen after the fact tells you little, because every handicapper has a hot stretch somewhere.
The leaderboard ranks experts by dollar profit over the last 7 days on a $100 bet size and shows no win and loss records. Seven days is far too short to separate skill from luck.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every SportsMemo pick with the line, odds and release time, and no third party audit.

What the seller publishes: a 7 day profit leaderboard, expert blurbs with selected runs, and a Yesterday's Plays page. When we opened Yesterday's Plays on 17 Nov 2026 it sent us to a WagerTalk login page, so we could not read it.

Older figures exist only as forum posts. In Nov 2009 an account posting as SportsMemo on the Las Vegas Advisor forum listed its newsletter at 211-155 (+37.0 units) in 2007, 202-174 (+9.7) in 2008 and 183-155 (+12.0) in 2009 through 16 Nov. Those are the seller's own numbers and we could not check them.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no SportsMemo pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how SportsMemo experts perform.
our_data.context: For scale: on the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent buyer talk about SportsMemo is thin and mostly old. The fullest threads are on the Las Vegas Advisor forum from 2009 and 2010. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found three relevant forum threads, all on the Las Vegas Advisor forum, from Sep 2009 to Dec 2010, and no recent buyer threads. The complaints repeat a few themes: a bad run of 27-77 over two Saturdays in late 2010 by one poster's count, a claim that picks once differed between the email and the website, trouble getting the release line, and a view that the site makes good runs easy to find and full records hard to find. On the positive side, one subscriber praised how the newsletter broke down games, members called two of its handicappers long term winners, and the site's own account posted yearly winning records for 2007 to 2009. Since WagerTalk bought it in 2018 we found almost nothing from buyers.

A Las Vegas Advisor member tallied the site's plays over the two previous Saturdays at 27-77, down 65.6 units, and argued that few paid handicappers beat -110 lines long term. A well known bettor replying in the thread called two days a cherry picked sample, while agreeing that long term winners are rare.

In the same thread, one member wrote that he stopped using a SportsMemo handicapper after picks were flipped by accident, with sides differing between the email and the website. Another said he often could not bet at the release number, and a third argued that the site promotes winning runs while full records are hard to find.

A thread opened by a member saying the SportsMemo best bets newsletter was down for the year drew mixed replies. One subscriber said the newsletter broke down games well but counted his own results at 56-52, down 1.2 units. Another was harsh about its NHL picks.

An account posting as SportsMemo replied in that thread that the newsletter was only slightly down for the football season and listed winning yearly totals for 2007 to 2009. It also gave its NHL writer's record as 20-24, down 10.15 units. These are the seller's figures.

In a thread about one SportsMemo handicapper, members split. One called him and another SportsMemo handicapper lifetime winners while warning that the second had some very poor years; another member said he saw no evidence either could hit 54% long term. The SportsMemo account posted multi year records in reply.

Our archive scan of the r/sportsbetting and r/sportsbook Reddit post streams found no buyer thread about SportsMemo, and our web searches found no SportsMemo thread on Sportsbook Review, TheRX or Covers. We did not check review sites that block automated reading.

conflicts: The leaderboard, the expert records and the Yesterday's Plays page are all run by the company that sells the picks. None is an independent audit.

SportsMemo is owned by Wager Talk Media, LP, which also runs WagerTalk. The refund page says card charges show as "WT/SM* PICKS AND PAR." One expert blurb cites rankings on Picks and Parlays and Winners and Whiners; we did not check who runs those sites.
strengths: A named parent company, a Las Vegas address and written terms under Nevada law.
Low entry prices: many single plays were $5.00 on 17 Nov 2026, so trying one expert costs little.
Prices are shown for each package before you buy, and the FAQ says you can cancel a subscription at any time.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a streak, a ranking or a 7 day board chosen and published by the seller.
All sales are final and nothing is guaranteed.
Many prices are shown as discounts from a higher regular price, which pushes quick decisions.
Old forum complaints mention picks that differed between email and website and lines that moved before buyers could bet.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the expert's last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Check whether you can still get the release line. A pick that only wins at the original number is worth less to you.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business founded in 2004, owned since 2018 by WagerTalk, with a named parent company, a Las Vegas address and written terms. We could not verify that its experts win over time, because the site does not publish a full, time stamped record of every pick.
On 17 Nov 2026 most single plays were $5.00, three day passes from two experts were $49, and one seven day all access pass was $77 with a coupon. Prices change daily.
Does SportsMemo have a verified record?
No. The site shows a 7 day profit leaderboard and selected runs in each expert's blurb, all published by SportsMemo. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

At $5 a play the price of the picks is small, but sales are final and nothing is guaranteed. What is unproven is whether any expert beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and nothing covers your betting losses.
